correctness.rationale: An irreducible symmetric Jacobi Hamiltonian has simple eigenvalues, so average mixing is the Gram matrix of squared real eigenvectors. Vandermonde inversion shows its rank equals that of diagonal moments W_{rj}=(H^r)_{jj}; resolvent adjugate expansion identifies that with span of vertex-deletion polynomials q_j. Unmarked q_j have full ceil(n/2) parity span. Their reflection differences split off tau and reduce, using U_n Chebyshev identities, to U_{n-2i} U_{j-1}^2 for j<=i and U_{i-1}^2 U_{n-2j} for j>i (up to reflection). Polynomial gcd U_{gcd(i,n+1)-1}, parity and degree constraints leave precisely floor((d-1)/2) dependencies. Centered odd marked paths retain reflection symmetry. An independently written exact SymPy diagonal-moment calculation checked 195 cases across n=2..11, all sites, and tau=-2,1/2,3/2. These finite checks corroborate rather than prove the all-n statement.

value.rationale: The exact gcd classification is a meaningful invariant of a natural one-marked graph: it settles positive definiteness and the rank deficiency for all path lengths, sites, and any nonzero potential without spectral-root approximation. It gives a sharp discontinuity from unmarked paths and tests general average-mixing-rank questions.

final_claim: For any unweighted path P_n, n>=2, one marked site i and any real tau!=0, the continuous-time quantum average-mixing matrix has rank (n+1)/2 if n odd and i central, otherwise n-floor((gcd(i,n+1)-1)/2); at tau=0 its rank is ceil(n/2). Full rank exactly when mark is noncentral and gcd<=2.
